reason: The text passage (2 Chronicles 18) actually demonstrates the opposite of the statement. It depicts Micaiah, a Hebrew prophet, explicitly refusing to be discouraged from expressing his authentic views. When pressured by the king's messenger to align with other prophets' favorable prophecies, Micaiah declares 'As the LORD lives, what my God says, that I will speak' (וַיֹּאמֶר מִיכָיְהוּ חַי־ יְהוָה כִּי אֶת־ אֲשֶׁר־ יֹאמַר אֱלֹהַי אֹתוֹ אֲדַבֵּר). Despite facing consequences—being struck and imprisoned—Micaiah remains resolute in voicing his unpopular prophecy. While the passage does show social and political pressure to conform, the primary narrative demonstrates courageous resistance to such discouragement rather than successful discouragement of expression.
